newsitem.title: SPAIN: EMU without Italy, Spain will be unstable -Prodi.
newsitem.headline: EMU without Italy, Spain will be unstable -Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who is due to meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl this morning, said on Thursday a European Monetary Union (EMU) without Italy and Spain would be unstable.

"France knows exactly that without Italy and Spain, the European Monetary Union would be reduced to a small mark area and the Union would be highly volatile," Prodi said in a interview published in the Spanish daily El Mundo.
He said France farmers and small firms wanted Italy in the Union.
"Farmers and small and medium sized firms in France are exactly the ones who would be most worried to see Italy and the lira out of EMU," Prodi said.
On Wednesday, the Financial Times newspaper reported that Italy would be offered a deal which would delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001.
But Prodi promptly denied there was any plan for Italy's late entry.

"This whole problem started in various public opinion polls which gave a very negative and traditional image of Italy -- an Italy of mandolins, mafia and political instability," he said in the El Mundo interview.

"For a weak politician it would be easy to conclude that in order to win elections it is necessary to tell German citizens that Italians will remain out of the Union, at least for a while. But Helmut Kohl is not a weak politician".
